name: Autonomous Chemistry
tagline: Robotics, machine learning, and self-driving labs shaping the future of synthesis.
seo_title: Autonomous Chemistry — paper summaries, news & innovations | Chemisters
seo_description: Follow Chemisters Autonomous Chemistry on LinkedIn and Facebook: paper summaries, news and innovations in self-driving labs, lab robotics, closed-loop optimization and AI lab agents.

definition.lead: Autonomous chemistry combines robotics, automation and AI so that experiments can be planned, run and analysed with little or no human intervention.
definition.body: In a self-driving lab, an algorithm chooses the next experiment, robots carry it out, instruments measure the result and the algorithm learns from it, around the clock. The goal is to discover molecules and materials many times faster than by hand.

timeline.title: Automated peptide synthesis
timeline.text: Bruce Merrifield and colleagues publish an instrument for automated peptide synthesis.
timeline.why: One of the first automated chemistry machines.

timeline.title: Automated DNA synthesis
timeline.text: Phosphoramidite chemistry from Marvin Caruthers's lab enables automated DNA synthesizers.

timeline.title: The robot scientist
timeline.text: Ross King's team reports 'Adam', which formed and tested hypotheses about yeast genes.
timeline.why: A machine that made discoveries on its own.

timeline.title: Searching for new reactivity
timeline.text: Lee Cronin's group uses a robot guided by machine learning to explore reactions.
timeline.why: Automation used for discovery, not just repetition.

timeline.title: The Chemputer
timeline.text: Cronin's group runs syntheses from a chemical programming language on a modular robot.

timeline.title: A mobile robot chemist
timeline.text: Andrew Cooper's team reports a robot that moves around a lab and runs 688 experiments in 8 days.

timeline.title: AI agents in the lab
timeline.text: Coscientist, a language-model agent, plans and runs chemistry experiments with lab hardware.
timeline.why: Large language models started operating lab equipment.

quiz.q: What is often the biggest bottleneck for self-driving labs?
options: Reliable automated handling of solids and purification, and data quality
Finding enough electricity to run robots all night
The cost of paper for printing experiment records
Keeping the lab at exactly room temperature
quiz.explain: Liquids are easy for robots; powders and workups are not.
